title: bug: the Claude Code plugin hook reads .moe/daemon.json with no size cap
description:
Objective: bound packages/moe-claude-plugin/src/daemonClient.ts readDaemonJson. The PostToolUse hook runs it on every moe.* tool call, and it reads the whole .moe/daemon.json with fs.readFileSync. This is a sibling of task-4f1e37f30ee548298b26e17c0b6ea84e (the JetBrains reader, 64 KiB cap). daemon.json is repository content, so a huge or never-ending file stalls every tool call.

Deliverable:
- A bounded read of at most 65537 bytes, with the descriptor closed on every path.
- A larger file returns null, like an unreadable one, so the hook stays fail-open: it takes the existing DAEMON_NOT_FOUND path and never throws into Claude Code.
- Valid files behave as today.

Not in scope: the walk-up project discovery, the hook's event forwarding, and the other clients, which have their own sibling tasks.

Verification: cd packages/moe-claude-plugin && npm test. On WSL its node_modules is a Windows install, so run vitest from a snapshot with a native npm ci. Never run npm run build in the shared checkout: the hook shim imports dist.
definitionOfDone: readDaemonJson accepts a valid 65536-byte daemon.json (JSON padded with spaces) and returns null for a 65537-byte one, proven by new tests/daemonClient.test.ts cases.
The read never takes more than 65537 bytes and closes its descriptor on every path, proven by a test.
An oversize daemon.json leaves the hook fail-open: no throw, and the existing not-found handling runs, proven by a test.
Fresh cd packages/moe-claude-plugin && npm test exits 0.

implementationPlan.note: RED in snapshot /tmp (npm ci there; shared checkout untouched): 4 failed (65537 boundary, bounded-read, EIO close, fail-open hook), 14 passed (65536 case + 13 existing). Other dirty paths belong to other sessions; not touched.

implementationPlan.description:
GREEN in packages/moe-claude-plugin/src/daemonClient.ts, next to readDaemonJson (~:101).

- Add const MAX_DAEMON_JSON_BYTES = 64 * 1024, with a one-line comment: daemon.json is repository content and the PostToolUse hook reads it on every moe.* tool call, so it is capped like the daemon, proxy and JetBrains readers.
- Add a private readDaemonJsonText(file: string): string | null:
  - const fd = fs.openSync(file, 'r') and one Buffer.alloc(MAX_DAEMON_JSON_BYTES + 1);
  - loop fs.readSync(fd, buf, total, buf.length - total, null) until it returns 0 or the buffer is full. A device or pipe can return short reads;
  - fs.closeSync(fd) in finally;
  - return null when total > MAX_DAEMON_JSON_BYTES, else buf.toString('utf8', 0, total).
  - Call fs.* through the existing default import, never named imports, which the test spies would not see.
- In readDaemonJson, inside the existing try, replace raw = fs.readFileSync(file, 'utf-8') with the helper. On null, return null.

Error handling stays as today: the existing catch turns any open or read error into null. So an oversize or unreadable file takes the same path as a missing or malformed one: the walk continues, findDaemonInfo throws DAEMON_NOT_FOUND, and runPostToolUseHook's catch logs it and returns send-failed. Nothing throws into Claude Code.

Unchanged: findDaemonInfo and its walk-up, readRecentProject (~/.moe/projects.json is user-home state, not repository content, and out of scope), callTool, postEvent, sendOnce, src/postToolUse.ts, hooks/post-tool-use.mjs and the README.

Re-run step 1's tests in the snapshot: green.
implementationPlan.note: GREEN: bounded readDaemonJsonText (MAX+1 read loop, close in finally); 18/18 in snapshot.

No bytes changed after gate. Residuals as planned (walk-up continues past oversize file; FIFO).

reopenReason: Human asked the architect seat to promote and plan the daemon.json size-cap follow-ups (2026-10-27).

planningNotes.approachesConsidered: (1) An fs.statSync size pre-check: rejected. A symlink to a device reports size 0. The read itself must be bounded, and test (2)'s exact read total catches a stat-only mutant. (2) A /dev/zero test: rejected. Against today's unbounded read it never ends and eats memory; it killed the daemon row's RED vitest worker. (3) Exporting readDaemonJson for direct tests: rejected. findDaemonInfo already exposes it, so the public surface stays as it is. (4) A distinct 'too large' error code for the hook: rejected. The task wants an oversize file to take the existing DAEMON_NOT_FOUND fail-open path, and the hook never surfaces the code anyway.
planningNotes.codebaseInsights:
- daemonClient.ts:101 readDaemonJson is the plugin's only daemon.json reader. It does existsSync, then readFileSync in a try that returns null, then JSON.parse and shape checks.
- findDaemonInfo walks up to 12 ancestors and throws DaemonError('DAEMON_NOT_FOUND').
- postToolUse.ts runPostToolUseHook catches any postEvent error, writes '[moe-claude-plugin] PostToolUse hook failed: <message>' to stderr, and returns { forwarded: false, reason: 'send-failed' }.
- npm test is plain vitest run (no pretest build). Tests import ../src/*.js directly.
- tsconfig excludes tests.
- In a scratch snapshot, vi.spyOn(fs, 'readFileSync') on the node:fs default import was verified to intercept daemonClient's calls.
planningNotes.risks:
- Do not build, clean or install in the shared checkout: the hook shim imports dist, and node_modules is shared with Windows.
- No /dev/zero test: runaway memory against the unfixed code.
- The cap is a cross-package contract: do not change 64 KiB here.
- The walk-up past an oversize file is pre-existing behavior, the same as for a malformed file, and out of scope.
